title: StreamFrame fidelity harness and model shim for function-call/backcompat testing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a repeatable regression harness that validates streaming frame-level fidelity, function-call boundary preservation, and structured-output JSON schema compatibility across model variants and runtime changes. This ticket implements a new lightweight model shim to emulate older function-call contracts and exercises it with a set of golden prompts and negative cases so the CI can detect accidental contract regressions before deploy.
acceptance_criteria: A harness exists that can replay 1k golden prompts and assert frame-level diffs (token boundaries, event types, error frames) in under 30 minutes on CI runners.
Function-call scenarios: shimmed older contract and current contract are exercised; differences are surfaced as structured diffs with root-cause suggestions.
Structured-output validator: JSON Schema + JSONPath checks run as part of tests; failures produce example failing output and minimal repro prompt.
CI gate: PRs that touch streaming, serializer, or func-call runtime code must run the harness and block on new failures (flaky-test backstop ticket created if flakiness > 5%).
Dashboard: an aggregated compatibility score on Console + a weekly digest to #runtime-alerts in Slack is available for the last 30 days of CI runs.
updates: 2025-02-20: Spike completed comparing current stream event model to legacy function-call wire contract; identified three mismatches in 'tool.end' framing.
2025-02-24: Implemented prototype shim that rewrites function-call events to legacy envelope for the harness; initial smoke tests passing locally (50/50 golden set).
2025-02-27: Design review with PM and DRI (Diego) — agreed to add explicit token-boundary assertions and to include deliberate timing jitter cases to catch race conditions.
2025-03-02: CI worker image updated (python-3.11 + rust-toolchain) and harness containerized; running nightly job against headless model snapshots for baseline collection.
2025-03-04: Discovered a flaky case around partial toolcall truncation on a long-prefix prompt; added deterministic seeding and a new failing golden prompt to the corpus.
notes: Harness must be easy to extend for future contract variants (e.g., multiplexed streams). Include metadata on each golden prompt describing expected model, tokenization assumptions, and chaos-injection knobs. Coordinate on rollout with Release Engineering to add CI quota for longer nightly baselines.
